briefHtml:
NAV S$10,255,679 — reported -0.47% (approx -0.09% real; Oct 14 base restated down to 10,265,307). Biggest mover: silver -~8% toward $56 after hot US core CPI — the watcher's silver/SILJ flags are REAL; the leveraged IBKR silver line lost ~11% of account equity in a day (now ~1.78x). Bright spot: Xiaomi +5.35% to HK$26.38 on ~1.8x volume. One thing: core CPI 2.6% y/y vs 2.5% exp doubled October hike odds to a coin flip and smashed metals — yet the 10y reversed to close LOWER at 5.19% and Treasury announced a $6bn buyback. The bond market is flinching at its own hawkishness; PPI + retail sales tonight is the next test.

State (fresh snapshot 07:40 SGT)

  • NAV S$10,255,679; reported -0.469%; listed sleeve -2.626% (contaminated by the stale SMIC flag). Oct 14 restated to 10,265,307. NAV level authoritative.
  • FX: USD/SGD 1.2841 (firmer post-CPI), CNY/SGD 0.192012 (USDCNY ~6.687), HKD/SGD 0.163623, MYR/SGD 0.314653.
  • priceErrors: L46.SI Yahoo 404 — 25th consecutive session.

Flag integrity — 1 stale, 3 real

  • SMIC -10.8% in a day (1.0% NW): stale — actual Wednesday close HK$54.30, -2.25%; -10.8% is the cumulative slide from Oct 7's 60.90.
  • SILJ -5.8% (0.8% NW): real — consistent with the post-CPI silver crash.
  • Silver IBKR -8.1% (1.2% NW): real — silver fell from ~$60.2 Asia morning to $56.23 (-4.68%) post-CPI.
  • Leveraged line equity ~-12.1%: real — collateral/equity now ~1.78x (from 1.70x).

Position moves

  • Asia Wed (pre-CPI): STI 5,423.33 -0.13%; HSI 24,314.17 -0.13%; Xiaomi 26.38 +5.35% on ~1.8x volume; SMIC 54.30 -2.25%; Tencent 423.40 -0.42%; DBS ~74.34 -0.17% (indicative).
  • US Wed (post-CPI): SPX 7,718.94 -1.11%; Nasdaq -1.88%; Dow -0.09%; VIX 16.87 +10.5%; 10y 5.19% (-3bp, full reversal of the spike); DXY 102.55 +0.3%. SOX -4.5% despite ASML's record quarter; Oracle -8.8%.
  • AI-credit scare: CoreWeave bond yield above 15% (distress levels); stock -15.5%.
  • Metals crash: gold below $4,100 ($4,093.87 -1.48%); silver $56.23 -4.68%; gold-silver ratio ~70.3. Oil: WTI ~$94.90 +1.1%.

Insider trades (7d)

  • Wing Tai (W05.SI): director change-of-interest filings Oct 12 (Buy-equivalent; same-day treasury-share transfer notice) and Oct 9 remain the latest in-window items; counts not disclosed.
  • Nothing new Oct 13-14; none for other SGX/HKEX held names. US holdings are ETFs — no insider filings exist.

Congress trades (filed Oct 13-14)

  • PA-9 (R): SOLD NVDA $1-15K (trade 8/31) — before the chip rout deepened.
  • OK-1 (R): big rotation out of equities into Oklahoma munis — sold NEE, ROK, SBUX, Virtus AI ETF, LMT x4, MRSH x2, CVX, DVN x2, EMR, HD, LIN.
  • CA-31 (D): ~60-line reshuffle; bought TSM, NXPI x2, ON Semi; sold AVGO, MCHP, MTSI x2, WDC, SMTC.
  • MI-9 (R): bought OLN, RIG, CACI, CAT, MSFT, Novagold (NG); SOLD STX $15-50K on 9/30 — days before the memory crash.
  • WA-2 (D): sold FDX, HD ($1-15K each); bought WSM.

Trump / policy watch (24-48h)

  • Hot core CPI 2.6% vs 2.5% exp (headline 3.7%; gasoline +9.1%); October hike odds ~doubled to ~43-50%, December ~95%. Fed split (Bowman calm, Goolsbee 'discouraging'). Treasury announced a $6bn buyback of 10-20y coupons. PPI + retail sales tonight; Warsh at IMF Friday.
  • Hormuz escalation — ships sinking: IRGC says a 2,500-container ship sank after hitting a mine; second vessel sank in ~24h; Houthi ballistic missile hit Riyadh airport; Aramco's Jeddah North station targeted. Netanyahu now opposes a pre-election Iran strike; Tehran in 'atmosphere of war'.
  • Russia-Ukraine: White House discusses cutting intel-sharing with Ukraine; Zelensky 'betrayed' by Trump's diesel deal; Novak touts 3.5M t/month diesel exports by year-end.
  • IEA October OMR: 2026 oil demand to fall 2.6M bpd (war disruption + prices), supply -5.8M bpd — stark divergence vs OPEC's +0.2M bpd growth view. SPR at 44-year low.
  • MAS HELD the S$NEER slope (Barclays had expected steepening); Singapore Q3 GDP +5.4% y/y with AI orders a key driver. China September credit strong: loans 1,080B, TSF 3,550B.
  • Trade: Germany pushing EU caps on Chinese imports; PBoC-BoJ meeting at IMF Bangkok; US troops to Latin America.

Risk

  • Silver line is the dominant risk: 1,777 oz x $56.2 x 1.2841 = ~S$128.3k collateral vs S$56,240 loan; equity ~S$72.0k (-~11% in a day); collateral/equity ~1.78x. A further -4% silver day = ~-7% equity. Hostage to tonight's PPI.
  • October hike now a coin flip; December ~95% priced — but 10y reversed lower and Treasury's buyback signals official discomfort at these yields.
  • AI-credit contagion risk: CoreWeave at 15% yields could de-rate the AI-bottleneck theme regardless of fundamentals.
  • FX: ~35% of NW non-SGD; USD/SGD firmed to 1.2841 — mild translation drag. Concentration: DBS ~2.2% NW. L46.SI feed down 25th session.

Alpha (signals, not advice; ~62% of liquid book still idle cash)

  • Real Assets (target 20%): silver flush was rates-driven, not thesis-breaking (Hormuz sinkings, SPR 44-yr low intact). Signal: silver stabilizing $55-56 while gold holds ~$4,100 = scale-in window; let line equity recover above ~1.8x before adding.
  • Xiaomi 1810.HK: +5.35% on 1.8x volume while SOX -4.5% and Congress dumped STX/WDC — BOM-relief divergence working; CXMT LPDDR6 for the foldable is the direct link. Signal: hold/build above ~HK$25.
  • Asia semis (SMIC/TSM) vs US AI-credit stress: CA-31 bought TSM into the rout; CoreWeave distress is a US-financing story, not Asia wafer utilization (SMIC 93.7%). Signal: SMIC holding ~HK$54 (Wed low 53.75) = semis-leg entry. Duration gate CLOSED — 10y 5.19% at, not below, 5.20% into PPI.

trumpWatch.title: Hot core CPI doubles October hike odds to a coin flip; Treasury announces $6bn buyback
trumpWatch.detail: Core CPI 2.6% y/y vs 2.5% exp (headline 3.7% vs 3.6%; energy +5.2%, gasoline +9.1%; real hourly earnings -0.7% y/y). October hike odds ~43-50% (from ~20-22%); December ~95% priced. Fed split: Bowman no urgency; Barkin 'higher than hoped'; Goolsbee 'discouraging'; Hassett blamed energy. Beige Book: little/no employment change. Treasury: preliminary $6bn liquidity-support buyback of 10-20y coupons. 10y reversed to close 5.19% (-3bp). PPI + retail sales Thursday; Warsh at IMF Bangkok Friday.

trumpWatch.title: Hormuz escalation: container ship sinks after mine strike; missiles on Riyadh and Jeddah
trumpWatch.detail: IRGC Navy: a 2,500-container ship sank south of Hormuz after hitting a naval mine; second commercial vessel sank near Hormuz in ~24h. Houthis hit Riyadh's King Khalid Int'l Airport with a ballistic missile; explosions in Jeddah as Aramco's Jeddah North distribution station was targeted. Netanyahu now opposes a pre-emptive Iran strike before elections; senior Iranian officials 'certain the US will attack' — 'atmosphere of war in Tehran'.

trumpWatch.title: Russia-Ukraine: White House weighs cutting intel-sharing; Zelensky 'betrayed' by diesel deal
trumpWatch.detail: Semafor: White House discussing cutting off intelligence-sharing with Ukraine; Ukraine hit two Russian refineries; Zelensky felt 'betrayed' by Trump's diesel deal with Russia; Novak: Russia could raise diesel exports to 3.5M t/month (~10% market share) by year-end.

trumpWatch.title: IEA vs OPEC: record divergence on 2026 oil demand
trumpWatch.detail: IEA October OMR: global oil demand to FALL 2.6M bpd in 2026 on Iran-war disruption and high prices; supply to fall 5.8M bpd to 100.7M bpd. OPEC's October MOMR sees +0.2M bpd demand growth. US SPR unchanged at 283M bbls — lowest since 1982.

trumpWatch.title: MAS holds S$NEER slope; Singapore Q3 GDP +5.4% on AI orders; China credit strong
trumpWatch.detail: MAS maintained the S$NEER appreciation rate, width and center unchanged (Barclays had expected a 25bp steepening). Q3 GDP +5.4% y/y (vs +6.2% Q2), +1.1% q/q SA; MAS sees core inflation slightly above 2%, easing discernibly from mid-2027. China September: new loans 1,080B vs 975B exp; TSF 3,550B vs 3,270B; M2 +7.2%.

trumpWatch.title: Trade/geopolitics: Germany pushes EU caps on Chinese imports; PBoC-BoJ to meet at IMF
trumpWatch.detail: Germany pushing the EU to cap additional Chinese imports; PBoC governor to meet BoJ counterpart at IMF Bangkok (Warsh speaks Friday); US sending several hundred Army soldiers to Latin America (NYT). Thursday data: Japan machinery orders, Korea trade, Australia jobs; US PPI + retail sales (survey +0.3% m/m vs +1.2% prior).

Rates-driven liquidation, not thesis break. Target: Real Assets 20% of book; ~62% of liquid book still idle cash.

opportunities.thesis: Memory rout = BOM relief, round 2: +5.35% on ~1.8x volume Wednesday WHILE SOX fell 4.5% and Congress members dumped STX/WDC (MI-9 sold STX 9/30, CA-31 sold WDC). CXMT confirmed as LPDDR6 supplier for Xiaomi's foldable — the direct input-cost link. IDC's China Q3 smartphone -15.4% is the bear case already in the price near HK$25.

CA-31 bought TSM into the rout — the same divergence.
opportunities.signal: SMIC holding ~HK$54 (Wednesday low 53.75) + TSM resilience = semis-leg entry. Duration gate for the Defense sleeve (target 15%) remains CLOSED — 10y at 5.19% is at, not below, 5.20% into PPI.
